svg.desc: Banner for a paper on stable twisted equilibria of the Kuramoto model on random geometric tori. In the centre, a square whose opposite edges are glued (a flat torus) holds 1,500 of the 4,096 randomly placed oscillators from the paper's numerical example, each dot coloured by its computed equilibrium phase on a colour wheel. The colours run once through the full wheel from left to right, so the phase winds once across the torus: the twist k = (1, 0). A colour bar above the square shows phase 0 to 2 pi. Left text: random points, stable twist. Right text: a computed equilibrium has phase equal to x plus a small correction, largest 0.27 radians; Theorem 2.1 states that, in every dimension, as the number of points grows with radius epsilon tending to zero and n epsilon to the power d+2 over log n tending to infinity, every twist k with |k| at most c/(epsilon+delta) has a stable equilibrium within C|k|delta of k.x at every point. A footnote says the picture is one numerical example (epsilon 0.6, seed 1404), an illustration outside the theorem's asymptotic regime.
